column1: # ZAP scan rule overrides for datawatch
# Format: <rule_id>\t<action>\t# justification
# Actions: IGNORE (suppress), WARN (default), FAIL (hard fail)
# Reviewed 2026-05-27. Each IGNORE below is a documented accepted risk
# or confirmed false positive — not a suppression of a real vulnerability.
# [10049] Non-Storable Content
# index.html is intentionally served with Cache-Control: no-store so the
# version-check script always loads the latest release. API responses also
# carry no-store to prevent stale authentication state. Intentional.

column3: Non-Storable Content — intentional no-store for version-check freshness

column1: # [10055] CSP: style-src unsafe-inline
# app.js generates HTML via template literals that include style="" attributes
# (e.g. dynamic width/height/color on session cards, heatmap cells, EKG
# canvas). Removing unsafe-inline requires converting ~200 inline-style sites
# to CSS classes — tracked as a future hardening item. script-src unsafe-inline
# has been eliminated via per-request nonces (v8.8.4). style-src is a lower
# risk because CSS cannot execute code.

column3: CSP style-src unsafe-inline — accepted; dynamic HTML templates use style="" attrs; script-src is nonce-protected

column1: # [10094] Base64 Disclosure
# SRI integrity="" attributes on CDN <script> and <link> tags contain SHA-384
# hashes encoded as base64. These are security features (subresource integrity),
# not sensitive data. ZAP cannot distinguish SRI hashes from secret content.

column3: Base64 Disclosure — false positive; values are SRI integrity hashes on CDN assets

column1: # [10109] Modern Web Application
# Informational finding. ZAP detected that the PWA is a modern single-page
# application. Not a vulnerability.

column3: Modern Web Application — informational only; not a vulnerability

column1: # [10112] Session Management Response Identified
# ZAP detected session-management behaviour in API responses (session IDs in
# JSON). This is expected and intentional for the session management API.

column3: Session Management Response — expected; datawatch API returns session IDs by design

column1: # [90004] Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy on CDN resources
# datawatch sets COEP: unsafe-none on all server responses (v8.8.4). ZAP also
# scans the CDN domains (cdnjs.cloudflare.com, cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpkg.com)
# which are third-party and outside operator control. The datawatch server
# itself correctly sets COEP.

column3: COEP on CDN resources — third-party CDNs outside operator control; datawatch server sets COEP: unsafe-none

column1: # [90005] Sec-Fetch-* Headers Missing
# Sec-Fetch-Dest/Mode/Site are browser-sent request headers. ZAP's finding
# means the server does not validate these headers to reject cross-origin
# requests. The PWA operates same-origin; frame-ancestors 'self' in CSP
# prevents cross-origin embedding. Adding Sec-Fetch validation is a future
# hardening item (defence-in-depth, not a current exploit path).

column3: Sec-Fetch-* Missing — server-side validation is defence-in-depth; CSP frame-ancestors guards embedding
